title: RIP, Tim Curry: Ars remembers his top 10 iconic performances
gist: A culture-desk obituary and career retrospective for actor Tim Curry, who died at 80; a pure entertainment/culture piece with no technology or investor-relevant content.

insights.claim: Actor Tim Curry died at his Los Angeles home at age 80; he had been in declining health and using a wheelchair since a 2012 stroke that required brain surgery, but continued working as an artist and writer afterward.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: No investor-relevant angle; purely a cultural obituary noting the death of a veteran actor.

insights.claim: The retrospective ranks Curry's most iconic roles, topped by Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975), which he originated on the London stage in 1973 and which remains the longest-running theatrical release film in history.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: No investor-relevant angle; the durability of Rocky Horror as a decades-long cult-film franchise is a cultural fact rather than a market signal.

insights.claim: The article notes a current Broadway revival of The Rocky Horror Show (with Luke Evans as Frank-N-Furter) has been nominated for nine Tony Awards, indicating continued commercial vitality of the franchise Curry originated.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A minor data point on ongoing licensing/revival value of a decades-old IP property, though not substantively investor-actionable from this article alone.
